bib.title: Coding Agents are Strong Prompt Optimizers

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Coding Agents are Strong Prompt Optimizers", Agamdeep Singh, Srishti Gautam, Priyanshu Gupta, Nikita Mehrotra, Tanmay Bakshi, Sumit Gulwani (Microsoft). arXiv 2609.26261v1 [cs.AI], stamped 13 Aug 2026. Preprint (AAAI-style format), 2026.
COVERAGE: FULL. 40,608 of 40,608 chars read (the /tmp extraction, 770 lines), covering abstract, body, limitations, conclusion and references. The PDF has 9 pages. There is no appendix. Figure captions were checked against figures.py. Page numbers below come from that caption run or are inferred, and are marked as such.

CENTRAL CLAIM: The search loop in prompt optimization (propose edit, fresh rollouts, score, keep if validation improves) is unnecessary. An unmodified coding agent (Claude Code, Claude Sonnet 5) is given a static corpus of agent trajectories and a one-paragraph instruction. It writes and runs analysis code over the whole corpus and writes a skill markdown file, which is used as the system prompt. The authors call this Coding-Agent Skill Distillation (CASD). They credit the gain to "reflection scope": corpus-wide statistics rather than minibatch reflection.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- CASD, one pass, beats GEPA on 3 of 4 benchmarks and SkillOpt on 4 of 4. All optimizers see only the same static rollout pool.
  number: mean gain over baseline +16.6 pts (CASD), +10.9 (GEPA), +5.3 (SkillOpt)
  setup: Table 1, limited-data regime. Target agent and user simulator are GPT-5.4-mini with reasoning disabled. Reflection LM for all methods is Claude Sonnet 5. Test accuracy is the mean over 3 seeds. Test sets: ALFWorld 50 held-out games (win rate); tau2-bench retail and telecom 40 held-out tasks each (pass@1); SpreadsheetBench-Verified 50 items (modified accuracy). Pool sizes: retail 35, telecom 50, SSB 50, ALFWorld 50.
  quote: "improving the unoptimized baseline by 16.6 percentage points on average versus 10.9 for GEPA and 5.3 for SkillOpt."
  where: abstract; Table 1; Sec 6.1
- Table 1 per-benchmark (mean ± sample SD, n-1): Baseline / CASD / SkillOpt / GEPA
  ALFWorld 56.7±1.2 / 83.3±2.3 / 68.0±2.0 (own scaffold, baseline 58.7, not directly comparable) / 74.0±2.0
  tau2 retail 32.5±2.5 / 40.0±2.5 / 38.3±10.1 / 39.2±7.2
  tau2 telecom 19.2±5.2 / 39.2±8.0 / 25.8±3.8 / 17.5±4.3
  SSB-Verified 39.3±3.1 / 51.3±3.1 / 38.7±2.3 / 60.7±3.1 (GEPA wins here)
  quote: "CASD is best on ALFWorld (83.3 vs. GEPA's 74.0), retail (40.0 vs. 39.2), and telecom (39.2 vs. 17.5), and second on SSB (51.3 vs. GEPA's 60.7)."
  where: Sec 6.1, p6
- GEPA falls below baseline on telecom when it has no external validation. The authors attribute this to overfitting on the pool it reflects on.
  number: 17.5 vs baseline 19.2; CASD +20.0
  setup: limited-data regime, telecom. GEPA budget 120 metric calls, Pareto set equal to train. Resuming to 240 calls gave a byte-identical prompt.
  quote: "GEPA's evolutionary loop degrades below baseline (17.5 vs. 19.2)—its edits are selected on the same pool it reflects on, and overfit—while the coding agent's statistics-first analysis of the identical data yields +20.0 points."
  where: Sec 6.1; settings in Sec 5
- Cost: about $1.60 per CASD prompt (one coding-agent session). The corpus is a byproduct of rollouts already generated, so there is no rollout bill. Table 3 totals over 4 benchmarks, in USD, with token caching on: CASD 6.4 (1.6 / 1.6 / 1.56 / 1.6), GEPA 8.4 (2.1 / 1.1 / 4.5 / 0.74), SkillOpt 142.5 (15.9 / 13.9 / 74.7 / 38.0). GEPA/SkillOpt telecom and SSB(SkillOpt) costs come from the head-to-head runs.
  quote: "Totaled over the four benchmarks this is 22× cheaper than SkillOpt ($142.5) and still less than GEPA ($8.4)"
  where: Sec 6.3, Table 3
- Head-to-head regime (Table 2): GEPA and SkillOpt also get a separate held-out validation set plus unrestricted environment rollouts; CASD is unchanged. CASD stays ahead on 2 of 4. Baseline / CASD / SkillOpt / GEPA: ALFWorld cells repeat the limited-data runs; retail 32.5 / 40.0 / 38.3±10.1 / 46.7±8.0; telecom 19.2 / 39.2±8.0 / 44.2±5.2 / 15.8±5.2; SSB 39.3 / 51.3 / 48.0±2.0 / 56.7±1.2. GEPA still fails on telecom (15.8). SkillOpt fixes telecom only at $74.7.
  quote: "Even when competing methods are granted additional validation data and unrestricted environment access, CASD remains ahead on two of four benchmarks."
  where: abstract; Sec 6.2
- Distilled skills recover test-time reasoning (Table 4, GPT-5.4-mini). no-think / +CASD / think: ALFWorld 56.7 / 83.3 / 71.3±1.2; retail 32.5 / 40.0 / 35.0±6.6; telecom 19.2 / 39.2 / 45.0±2.5 (78% of the gap recovered); SSB 39.3 / 51.3 / 61.3±1.2 (55% recovered). Output tokens per episode, think to skill: 3.7k to 0.8k, 1.6k to 0.6k, 2.1k to 0.6k, 3.3k to 0.8k. Think-mode accuracies and token counts are from an earlier study on the same test splits. The exception is SSB think, which used a different harness and is "indicative".
  quote: "on telecom and SSB it recovers 78% and 55% of the no-think→think gap. It does so while emitting zero reasoning tokens: per-episode output stays at or below the no-think budget (0.6–0.8k tokens), where thinking costs 2.9–4.5× more."
  where: Sec 6.5, Table 4 and footnote 1
- A distillation corpus built from think rollouts is not needed. In the earlier study round, distilling from think rollouts versus no-think rollouts landed within a few points of each other, with no consistent winner. Examples: ALFWorld 81.3 vs 78.7; retail 45.8 vs 40.8; telecom 32.5 vs 33.3; SSB 46.0 vs 56.0.
  quote: "ALFWorld 81.3 think-distilled vs. 78.7 no-think-distilled; retail 45.8 vs. 40.8; telecom 32.5 vs. 33.3; SSB reversed, 46.0 vs. 56.0"
  where: Sec 6.5
- What the distiller does, from 24 logged distillation runs (816 tool calls). A hand classification gives 94 exploring the layout, 184 computing corpus statistics, 510 inspecting episodes and 28 writing the skill. Runs have 16–51 tool calls (mean 34.0) and produce a 5–8KB skill file. Runs switch between statistics and inspection a median of 5 times (up to 16). Every run measures rewards/pass rates and episode lengths. 96% quantify termination and failure modes, 92% analyse tool usage, 79% break down by task category, and one third search for duplicated tool calls.
  quote: "the 12 CASD skills contain 54 quantitative evidence citations (fractions, percentages, and measured counts; 4.6 per 1k words, Figure 2c), compared with none across the four GEPA prompts and only one across the four SkillOpt prompts."
  where: Sec 3.3, p4
- Mechanism examples. The telecom skill's top rule targets fabricated identity-lookup arguments seen in 16/50 episodes (32%). get_details_by_id was called 284 times, with 123 exact duplicates. An entire task category failed 24 of 24 attempts. In the Figure 4 case study, a billing root cause appears only as an absence (make_payment is never called in the pool). Only CASD writes a rule for it and solves the episode.
  quote: "Detecting that 123 of 284 get_details_by_id calls were exact duplicates requires joining tool calls across a whole episode set—a one-liner in pandas, but invisible in a context-window reflection."
  where: Sec 6.4, p6–7
- Variance. SkillOpt retail SD is 10.1 and GEPA retail SD is 7.2. CASD SD is at most 3.1 on 3 of 4 benchmarks (telecom is 8.0).
  quote: "its variance across independently produced skills is small (SD≤3.1 on 3 of 4 benchmarks)."
  where: Sec 6.4
- Theory, not tested empirically. The unified update is p_{t+1} = Π[p_t ⊕ ρ(p_t, φ_t)] (Eq 1). Search feedback is a Monte Carlo validation estimate with Var = σ²/|D_val| (Eq 2). CASD feedback is deterministic corpus statistics plus a set of inspected trajectories (Eq 3). The authors predict that CASD wins under small rollout budgets (lower variance, but bias from a fixed corpus), and that search wins as budget grows.
  quote: "Offline distillation is particularly well suited to budget-constrained optimization, whereas iterative search is expected to benefit more from abundant interaction budgets."
  where: Sec 4.2–4.3
- Prompt-length cost at deployment: on telecom, SkillOpt's prompt induces 20.1M prompt tokens over the 3-seed evaluation, versus 11.9M for GEPA's.
  quote: "SkillOpt's prompt induces 20.1M prompt tokens over the 3-seed evaluation versus 11.9M for GEPA's"
  where: Sec 6.3

THE INSTRUCTION (verbatim, Sec 3.2): "There is a results file here containing N agent rollout trajectories for [task family]. Analyze it directly—no other inputs, no precomputed summaries—and distill a skill markdown file capturing the behavioral rules that would make a future agent instance more accurate and more token/step-efficient on this task family. Use your own judgment fully on methodology. Write the skill file into this directory."

BASELINE SETTINGS: GEPA has a budget of 120 metric calls. SkillOpt runs 3–5 epochs, minibatch 8–40, edit budget 4 per step cosine-decayed to 2, and a validation gate on. Its internal split in the limited-data regime is 25/10 on retail and 35/15 elsewhere. CASD synthesises 3 skills per benchmark and reports their mean. MIPRO, OPRO and APE are not run as baselines; they appear only in related work.

LIMITS
- Conceded by the authors:
  - The CASD SD is skill-to-skill (3 distilled skills, one evaluation each). The baseline SD is seed-to-seed for a single prompt, so the two are "close but not identical".
  - There is one target model (GPT-5.4-mini, no-think) and one coding agent (Claude Sonnet 5 / Claude Code). Sensitivity to distiller capability is untested.
  - CASD "cannot discover behaviors absent from the logged rollouts", and small or failure-free corpora may leave nothing to distill. (The Figure 4 absence case needs a corpus that shows what was never done.)
  - Residual gaps on telecom and SSB: the authors suggest instance-specific deduction that no static prompt recovers.
  - The authors note the binomial standard error alone is about 7 points per seed at these test-set sizes.
- Not shown, my reading of the text:
  - Many headline gaps are within noise. Retail 40.0 vs 39.2 (CASD vs GEPA) is inside SDs of 2.5 and 7.2. Telecom head-to-head is described as "within noise".
  - There are only 3 seeds and 3 skills, with no significance tests.
  - Only 4 benchmarks, all agentic. There are no single-turn tasks, and no APE/OPRO-style instruction tuning on classification or QA.
  - GEPA wins SSB in both regimes (60.7 and 56.7 vs CASD 51.3). SkillOpt wins telecom head-to-head (44.2).
  - The ALFWorld SkillOpt number uses its native scaffold, so it is not comparable.
  - Table 2 ALFWorld cells are copies of Table 1.
  - Think-mode numbers come from an earlier study (SSB think uses a different harness).
  - The cost of generating the rollout corpus is excluded from CASD's $1.60. The paper argues it is a byproduct. Costs include token caching.
  - GEPA's budget is a single 120-call point (240 gave an identical prompt on telecom).
  - The bias-variance argument is not tested directly (no corpus-size or budget sweep).
  - No held-out transfer beyond the same task family.
  - The same optimizer LM (Sonnet 5) is used for all methods, but CASD gets the agentic tool-using harness while the baselines use their native reflection.
  - Authors are at Microsoft, and GEPA's authors are a separate group.

BUILDS ON (as printed)
- Search-based prompt optimization: Zhou et al. 2023 (APE); Yang et al. 2024a (OPRO); Pryzant et al. 2023 (ProTeGi); Khattab et al. 2024 (DSPy); Opsahl-Ong et al. 2024 (MIPRO); Shin et al. 2020 (AutoPrompt); Yuksekgonul et al. 2024 (TextGrad); Cheng, Nie and Swaminathan 2024 (Trace); Fernando et al. 2023 (Promptbreeder); Guo et al. 2024 (EvoPrompt); Wang et al. 2024b (PromptAgent, MCTS); Agrawal et al. 2026 (GEPA, ICLR). SkillOpt is used as a baseline without a citation in the extraction.
- Experience without weight updates: Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023); Self-Refine (Madaan et al. 2023); Voyager (Wang et al. 2024a); ExpeL (Zhao et al. 2024); Agent Workflow Memory (Wang et al. 2025b); Generative Agents (Park et al. 2023); Dynamic Cheatsheet (Suzgun et al. 2026); ReasoningBank (Ouyang et al. 2025); ACE (Zhang et al. 2025).
- Method inspiration: program-aided reasoning for exact counting (PAL, Gao et al. 2023; Program of Thoughts, Chen et al. 2023), applied to the optimizer. Offline RL conservatism (Levine et al. 2020; BCQ, Fujimoto et al. 2019; CQL, Kumar et al. 2020; one-step methods, Brandfonbrener et al. 2021). Coding agents: SWE-agent (Yang et al. 2024b), OpenHands (Wang et al. 2025a), Claude Code (Anthropic 2025).
- Benchmarks: ALFWorld (Shridhar 2021); tau2-bench (Barres 2026); tau-bench (Yao 2024); SpreadsheetBench (Ma 2024); ReAct scaffold (Yao 2023). Overfitting: Smith and Winkler 2006; Dwork et al. 2015. Error bars: Miller 2024.

CODE: none beyond the Sec 3.2 instruction above. The paper has no code listing or code-release statement in the extracted text.

FIGURES (page numbers from figures.py captions)
- Fig 1 (p2): left, search-based loop (GEPA, SkillOpt) vs CASD's single offline pass over a frozen corpus; right, average gain vs optimization cost. Shows the whole contrast and the headline in one image.
- Fig 2 (p4): "Inside the distiller". (a) tool traces over 24 runs: front-loaded exploration, terminal writing, alternating stats/inspection. (b) which corpus statistics are computed. (c) quantitative-evidence citations per prompt.
- Fig 3 (p6): bar chart of Table 1 (mean with SD whiskers, 3 seeds). Shows the SD overlaps.
- Fig 4 (p7): telecom case study. The same 50-rollout pool distilled by the three optimizers into different prompts. The billing rule exists only as an absence (make_payment never called), and only CASD finds it. This is the most concrete explanation of why corpus scope matters.
- Tables 1–4 hold the key numbers.

PROBLEMS: The extraction has some missing spaces from the PDF text layer (for example "Search-basedpromptoptimizers"); numbers and tables are intact. Line 1 of the /tmp file reads "9 pages", which is a page count (the PDF has 9 pages). The arXiv ID 2609.* conflicts with the stamped date 13 Aug 2026 (2609 would be Sept 2026). I did not resolve this, so check the ID before citing it. SkillOpt has no reference entry in the extracted bibliography. No embedded instructions were found in the text. The Sec 3.2 quoted prompt is the paper's own method, not an instruction to me.
